description: Curated papers with no local PDF. Hand-maintained; extract_papers.py never writes this file. Each url was verified against the arXiv API (title + ID match) when added.

papers.title: Agent Skills for Large Language Models: Architecture, Acquisition, Security, and the Path Forward
papers.note: Four-axis survey: architectural foundations (SKILL.md, progressive context loading, MCP integration), skill acquisition, deployment at scale (CUAs, OSWorld), and security frameworks.
papers.type_evidence: this survey provides a comprehensive treatment of the agent skills landscape

papers.title: SoK: Agentic Skills -- Beyond Tool Use in LLM Agents
papers.note: Systematization of knowledge mapping how skills transcend basic function-calling and tool-use paradigms, across the full skill lifecycle.
papers.type_evidence: this paper maps the skill layer and introduces two complementary taxonomies

papers.title: Trace2Skill: Distill Trajectory-Local Lessons into Transferable Agent Skills
papers.note: Turns single-run execution trajectories into reusable, generalized agent skills; harness-agnostic.
papers.type_evidence: distill trajectory-local lessons into transferable agent skills

papers.title: Externalization in LLM Agents: A Unified Review of Memory, Skills, Protocols and Harness Engineering
papers.note: Examines how externalized artifacts (skills, workflow memory, protocols) substitute or complement internal model weights.
papers.type_evidence: a unified review of memory, skills, protocols and harness engineering

papers.title: Skilldex: A Package Manager and Registry for Agent Skill Packages with Hierarchical Scope-Based Distribution
papers.note: Package management and hierarchical scope distribution (global/shared/project) for agent skill artifacts, with format conformance scoring.
papers.type_evidence: a package manager and registry, implemented as a TypeScript CLI with a registry backend

papers.title: Code as Agent Harness
papers.type_evidence: we organize the survey around three connected layers; this survey provides a unified roadmap
papers.note: Frames code as the operational substrate of agent harnesses across three layers (interface, mechanisms, scaling to multi-agent); covers coding assistants, GUI/OS automation, embodied agents, DevOps.

papers.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
papers.note: Treats skill files as trainable parameters outside frozen model weights via bounded text edits, validation gating, and rejected-edit feedback. Often cited by its Microsoft Research blog title, 'Agent Skills as Trainable Parameters'.
papers.type_evidence: treats a skill file as a trainable parameter outside a frozen model

papers.title: Agent Skill Evaluation and Evolution: Frameworks and Benchmarks
papers.note: Automated, evaluation-driven skill evolution via execution feedback, trajectory distillation, compression, and RL; plus six skill-centric benchmark categories.
papers.type_evidence: in this survey, we systematically examine the landscape of skill evolution

papers.title: GitSkills: A Dataset of Agent Skills on GitHub
papers.note: 3,797,117 SKILL.md files from 282,200 public repositories, grouped into 1,877,981 distinct contents, shipped as a single searchable SQLite file.
papers.type_evidence: 3.8M SKILL.md files from 282k repos, shipped as one searchable SQLite file

papers.title: Agent Skills Can Be Harmful: An Empirical Study of Skill-Induced Failures in LLM Agents
papers.note: 307 skill-induced failures on SkillsBench and SWE-Skills-Bench (125 functional, 182 efficiency); excessive procedural checklists and heavy implementation pipelines cut success rates and inflate cost.
papers.type_evidence: differential analysis framework instantiated on existing SkillsBench, yielding 307 failures

papers.title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't
papers.note: Contrastive study of 8,135 trial records: skills act as procedural anchors (65.7%) rather than injecting missing facts (4.5%); retrieval precision falls from 29.6% to 3.3% as pools grow 5 to 100.
papers.type_evidence: when do skills help, why do they work, where do they fail; controlled contrastive study

papers.title: SkillAlign: Aligning Skill Interfaces for LLM-based Agents
papers.type_evidence: we propose SkillAlign, a provider-agnostic framework rendering skills through alternative exposure interfaces
papers.note: The same skill can help or mislead depending on how it is exposed: full instructions, hints, summaries, workflows, or none. Exposure form swings ALFWorld success from 47.9% to 72.1%; compact top-k can beat full-library injection.

papers.title: Skill Constellations: Tracing the Supply Chain of Agent Skills on GitHub
papers.type_evidence: first dated copy network of agent skills, 2,193,119 adoptions; auditing its top-100 repos prevents 14.9% of high-risk adoptions vs 0.5% for most-starred
papers.note: Skill sharing is a supply chain with no registry, versions, or provenance. A few repos are the source of almost all copies and stars do not identify them; copies almost never track their source, so a fix at the source rarely reaches them.
